title: Fluids and electrolytes
summary: Choose and prescribe IV fluids as drugs (balanced crystalloids for most), and manage the electrolyte emergencies of the ICU: hypo- and hypernatraemia with safe correction limits, hyperkalaemia, hypokalaemia, and calcium, magnesium and phosphate disorders including refeeding syndrome.

topics.title: IV fluids: choice, dose and stewardship
topics.summary: Treat fluids as drugs with four phases: resuscitation, optimisation, stabilisation, de-escalation. Balanced crystalloids are reasonable default resuscitation fluids; saline for TBI and hypochloraemia; albumin selectively; never starches.

definition.text: Four indications: resuscitation, replacement of ongoing losses, maintenance (often unnecessary when enteral feed and drug diluents already cover water needs), and nutrition.

steps.title: Bolus and reassess
steps.detail: 250-500 mL balanced crystalloid over 15-30 min; reassess perfusion and fluid responsiveness (PLR, POCUS) before each further bolus.

steps.title: Balanced vs saline
steps.detail: SMART (n = 15,802) showed fewer major adverse kidney events with balanced fluids; PLUS and BaSICS showed no mortality difference. Balanced fluids are a reasonable default.

steps.title: Use 0.9% saline
steps.detail: Severe TBI / raised ICP (BaSICS signal of harm with balanced fluid in TBI), hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis, hyponatraemia.

steps.title: Adult needs
steps.detail: Water 25-30 mL/kg/day, Na+ 1 mmol/kg, K+ 1 mmol/kg, glucose 50-100 g/day; count all drug infusions and feeds (fluid creep).

steps.title: Once stable
steps.detail: Stop maintenance fluid, concentrate infusions, target even or negative balance; diuretics or RRT for overload.

tables.title: Composition of common IV fluids (mmol/L)
tables.caption: Values vary slightly by manufacturer; check the bag. Hydroxyethyl starch is associated with AKI and death in sepsis and should not be used.

redFlags.text: Lung crackles, rising oxygen need, B-lines or a plethoric non-collapsing IVC after boluses: stop fluid.

pitfalls.text: Running 'maintenance' DNS at 100 mL/h by default in a patient already on enteral feeds and multiple drug infusions.
Hypotonic fluids (dextrose-saline, 5% dextrose) as maintenance in sick patients → hospital-acquired hyponatraemia.

pearls.text: Write the fluid order as a drug: type, volume, rate, indication, review time.

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **SMART 2018:** balanced vs saline, MAKE30 14.3% vs 15.4%.
- **PLUS 2022:** Plasma-Lyte vs saline, 90-day mortality 21.8% vs 22.0%.
- **BaSICS 2021:** no overall difference; possible harm with balanced fluid in TBI.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Benefit of balanced fluids is small; meta-analyses suggest a modest reduction in mortality but the confidence interval includes no effect.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - RL is cheap and universally available; Plasma-Lyte costs more. DNS remains overused as "maintenance" in Indian wards; this is a common source of hyponatraemia and hyperglycaemia.

topics.title: Hyponatraemia
topics.summary: Treat symptoms, not the number: severe symptoms get 3% saline boluses immediately. Then classify by osmolality, volume status and urine studies. Limit correction to 10 mmol/L in 24 h (8 if high risk of osmotic demyelination) and re-lower if overshooting.

definition.text: Serum Na+ < 135 mmol/L. Mild 130-134, moderate 125-129, profound < 125 (European guideline).

steps.title: Severe symptoms?
steps.detail: Vomiting, seizures, GCS < 9, cardiorespiratory distress: 150 mL 3% saline over 20 min, check Na+, repeat up to twice until Na+ rises 5 mmol/L.

steps.title: Single bolus
steps.detail: Confusion, nausea, headache: one 150 mL 3% bolus (or 2 mL/kg), then treat cause; target +5 mmol/L/24 h.

steps.title: Rule out pseudo/translocational
steps.detail: Measure serum osmolality and glucose (correct Na+ for hyperglycaemia); exclude hyperlipidaemia/paraprotein, mannitol.

steps.title: Urine osmolality and Na+
steps.detail: Uosm < 100 → water excess (primary polydipsia, beer potomania, low solute). UNa < 30 → low effective arterial volume (GI loss, heart failure, cirrhosis). UNa > 30 → SIADH, diuretics, adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, cerebral salt wasting.

steps.title: By cause
steps.detail: Hypovolaemia: 0.9% saline or RL. SIADH: fluid restriction < 800-1000 mL/day; oral urea 15-30 g/day or salt tablets + furosemide if refractory. Heart failure/cirrhosis: fluid restriction, treat underlying.

steps.title: Every 4-6 h
steps.detail: Limit rise to 10 mmol/L in first 24 h and 8 mmol/L in each subsequent 24 h; in high-risk patients aim for 4-8 and do not exceed 8. Watch for aquaresis (UO > 100 mL/h).

steps.title: Re-lower
steps.detail: Stop hypertonic fluid; 5% dextrose 10 mL/kg over 1 h ± desmopressin 1-2 mcg IV/SC to bring Na+ back below the limit.

doseCards.dose: 150 mL over 20 min; repeat up to 2 more times guided by Na+ (or 2 mL/kg, max 150 mL)
doseCards.target: Rise of 5 mmol/L in the first 1-2 h; symptoms improve
doseCards.workedExample: 60 kg woman, Na+ 112, seizing: 150 mL 3% over 20 min → Na+ 115; repeat 150 mL → 117; stop boluses
doseCards.notes: SALSA: rapid intermittent boluses had no more overcorrection than slow continuous infusion.

tables.title: High risk of osmotic demyelination: correct more slowly
rows: Common in Indian men with beer potomania
tables.caption: US expert panel: in high-risk patients, aim for 4-8 mmol/L per day and do not exceed 8 mmol/L in any 24 h.

redFlags.text: Seizure or GCS fall with Na+ < 125: hypertonic saline now, not a water restriction.
Urine output suddenly > 100 mL/h of dilute urine: overcorrection is coming; check Na+ every 1-2 h.

pitfalls.text: Giving 0.9% saline in SIADH (urine osmolality > 500): Na+ may fall further.
Forgetting that K+ replacement also raises Na+.
Missing adrenal insufficiency or hypothyroidism before labelling SIADH.

pearls.text: Urine osmolality + urine Na+ before treatment are worth more than any formula.
Thiazides are a leading cause in the elderly; stop them.

nodes.text: 3% saline 150 mL over 20 min; repeat to +5 mmol/L
Water excess / low solute: restrict water; watch rapid correction
Low effective volume: saline if hypovolaemic; restrict if HF/cirrhosis
SIADH, diuretics, adrenal, thyroid: check cortisol/TSH; fluid restriction

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: - Brain cells adapt within 48 h by losing osmolytes; rapid correction then dehydrates them, causing osmotic demyelination 2-6 days later.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- **European guideline 2014** and **US expert panel 2013** agree on 3% bolus therapy for severe symptoms and on daily limits.
- **SALSA 2021:** rapid intermittent bolus vs slow continuous infusion: similar overcorrection rates.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Tolvaptan: effective in SIADH but costly, risk of overcorrection and liver injury; avoid in liver disease.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Common Indian causes: thiazides, diarrhoeal illness, beer potomania, SIADH from TB meningitis/pneumonia, hypothyroidism and hypopituitarism (Sheehan's syndrome in women).

topics.title: Hypernatraemia
topics.summary: Na+ > 145 mmol/L usually means water loss plus inability to drink. Restore volume first if shocked, then replace the free-water deficit plus ongoing losses, lowering Na+ by about 10 mmol/L/day in chronic cases.

steps.title: Volume
steps.detail: Shock or hypovolaemia: isotonic crystalloid boluses first.

steps.title: Classify
steps.detail: Renal water loss (osmotic diuresis from glucose/urea/mannitol, diabetes insipidus), GI/insensible losses, or sodium gain (hypertonic saline, bicarbonate). Urine osmolality < 300 with polyuria suggests DI.

steps.title: Free water
steps.detail: Enteral water via NG tube is best; IV 5% dextrose or 0.45% saline. Use the free-water deficit or Adrogué-Madias formula and add ongoing losses.

steps.title: Chronic (> 48 h)
steps.detail: Lower Na+ by ≤ 10-12 mmol/L per 24 h to avoid cerebral oedema; acute (hours, e.g. salt ingestion) can be corrected faster.

steps.title: Central
steps.detail: Desmopressin 1-2 mcg IV/SC (or 10 mcg intranasal) and replace losses; common after neurosurgery, TBI, brain death.

redFlags.text: Hypernatraemia in an ICU patient on diuretics and hypertonic fluids is iatrogenic until proven otherwise.

pitfalls.text: Treating with 0.9% saline alone, which is hypertonic relative to the urine in osmotic diuresis.
Forgetting glucose load with large 5% dextrose volumes.

pearls.text: 1 L of 5% dextrose lowers Na+ by about (Na+ − 0)/(TBW + 1): use sodium-change-per-litre.

nodes.text: Free water deficit + ongoing losses; ≤ 10-12 mmol/L/day

consultantNotes.evidence: - **Adrogué & Madias 2000:** classic review; formula for change in Na+ per litre of infusate.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Observational data in adults suggest faster correction (> 0.5 mmol/L/h) is not clearly harmful, but the 10-12 mmol/day limit remains standard practice.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Elderly patients with poor water access and fever in summer, heat illness, and post-neurosurgical DI are common scenarios.

topics.title: Hyperkalaemia
topics.summary: Five steps (UKKA): protect the heart with IV calcium if ECG changes, shift K+ into cells with insulin-glucose (± salbutamol), remove K+ (binders, diuresis, dialysis), monitor glucose and K+, and prevent recurrence.

steps.title: ECG and confirm
steps.detail: 12-lead ECG, continuous monitoring; repeat sample if haemolysed but do not delay treatment if ECG changes.

steps.title: Protect the heart
steps.detail: ECG changes: 30 mL 10% calcium gluconate over 10 min (10 mL 10% calcium chloride over 5 min in peri-arrest). Repeat if changes persist after 5-10 min.

steps.title: Shift K+
steps.detail: K+ ≥ 6.0: soluble insulin 10 units + 25 g glucose over 15 min. If pre-treatment glucose < 7 mmol/L (126 mg/dL): then 10% glucose 50 mL/h for 5 h. K+ ≥ 6.5: add salbutamol 10-20 mg nebulised.

steps.title: Remove K+
steps.detail: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g three times daily (or patiromer); loop diuretic if passing urine and volume replete; urgent dialysis for refractory hyperkalaemia, anuric AKI or ESKD.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.detail: K+ at 1, 2, 4, 6 and 24 h; capillary glucose 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360 min after insulin.

steps.title: Prevent
steps.detail: Stop K+ supplements, ACEi/ARB/MRA, NSAIDs, trimethoprim, heparin; treat rhabdomyolysis, tumour lysis, acidosis.

doseCards.dose: 30 mL of 10% over 10 min; repeat if ECG unchanged
doseCards.notes: Onset 3 min, lasts 30-60 min; does not lower K+.

doseCards.dose: Soluble insulin 10 units + 25 g glucose (50 mL 50% or 250 mL 10%) over 15 min
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg, K+ 7.1, glucose 90 mg/dL (5 mmol/L): insulin 10 units + 50 mL 50% dextrose; then 10% dextrose 50 mL/h for 5 h
doseCards.verify: Draw 10 units with an insulin syringe of the correct strength (U-40 vs U-100).

tables.title: ECG changes of hyperkalaemia (not reliably sequential)
rows: Bradycardia, high-grade AV block, junctional rhythm
Cardiac arrest: calcium chloride, insulin-glucose, consider bicarbonate, dialysis
tables.caption: BRASH syndrome (Bradycardia, Renal failure, AV nodal blockade, Shock, Hyperkalaemia) can occur with K+ < 6.5.

redFlags.text: Broad QRS or bradycardia with high K+: calcium now, then everything else.

pitfalls.text: Hypoglycaemia hours after insulin, especially in CKD (no glucose monitoring).
Relying on sodium polystyrene / calcium resonium for acute treatment (slow; not recommended).
Sodium bicarbonate as routine therapy: insufficient evidence except in cardiac arrest or severe acidosis.

pearls.text: Calcium gluconate 30 mL of 10% contains the same calcium as 10 mL of 10% chloride.

nodes.text: Insulin 10 U + glucose 25 g; salbutamol if K+ ≥ 6.5
Glucose monitoring for 6 h; 10% glucose 50 mL/h × 5 h if baseline < 7 mmol/L
Re-check K+ at 1, 2, 4, 6, 24 h; prevent recurrence

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **UKKA 2023 (updated 2026):** calcium gluconate dose increased to 30 mL; insulin-glucose with structured glucose monitoring; calcium resonium removed from acute algorithm.
- **KDIGO 2020:** consensus on potassium homeostasis and dyskalaemia.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Lower insulin doses (5 units) in CKD reduce hypoglycaemia but may be less effective.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate is available in India but costly; patiromer availability is limited. Dialysis access drives management in district hospitals.

topics.title: Hypokalaemia
topics.summary: Replace potassium safely (≤ 10 mmol/h peripherally, ≤ 20 mmol/h centrally with monitoring), correct magnesium, and look for the cause (GI loss, diuretics, insulin, β-agonists, refeeding, RTA, hyperaldosteronism).

steps.title: Severity
steps.detail: Mild 3.0-3.4; severe < 2.5 or with ECG changes (U waves, ST depression, arrhythmia), weakness or paralysis, digoxin, or cardiac disease.

steps.title: Oral if possible
steps.detail: KCl 20-40 mmol 2-3 times daily.

steps.title: IV
steps.detail: Peripheral up to 10 mmol/h (concentration ≤ 40 mmol/L); central with ECG monitoring up to 20 mmol/h. Each 10 mmol raises K+ ~0.1 mmol/L (less with ongoing losses).

steps.title: Always check
steps.detail: Hypomagnesaemia causes refractory hypokalaemia; give 2 g magnesium sulphate IV.

steps.title: Urine K+
steps.detail: Urine K+ < 20 mmol/day (or K/creatinine low) → GI/shift; high → renal loss (diuretics, vomiting, RTA, hyperaldosteronism).

doseCards.route: IV via central line, cardiac monitor
doseCards.dose: 20 mmol in 100 mL over 1 h; repeat with K+ checks
doseCards.workedExample: K+ 2.4 with ectopics: 20 mmol/h centrally ×2, re-check; + 2 g MgSO4 over 30 min
doseCards.verify: Check whether central concentrated KCl is permitted on your unit's policy.

redFlags.text: Flaccid paralysis with K+ < 2.5: hypokalaemic periodic paralysis, distal RTA, or Gitelman; ventilatory failure is possible.

pearls.text: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis: Asian men, high carbohydrate meal; small K+ doses + propranolol to avoid rebound hyperkalaemia.

consultantNotes.evidence: - **KDIGO 2020 controversies conference:** consensus on potassium homeostasis; IV replacement rates reflect standard safety practice rather than trials.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Diarrhoeal illness and diuretics are the commonest causes; hypokalaemic paralysis presents frequently to Indian emergency departments, including distal RTA and thyrotoxic periodic paralysis.

quiz.explanation: Higher rates need a central line and monitoring.
Low Mg drives renal K+ loss.

topics.title: Calcium, magnesium, phosphate and refeeding syndrome
topics.summary: Use ionised calcium in the ICU. Treat symptomatic hypocalcaemia with IV calcium; replace magnesium early. Identify refeeding risk before feeding: start low, give thiamine, and check phosphate, potassium and magnesium every 12 h for 3 days.

steps.title: Measure ionised
steps.detail: Normal iCa 1.1-1.3 mmol/L. Total calcium correction for albumin is unreliable in ICU.

steps.title: Symptomatic
steps.detail: Tetany, seizures, prolonged QT, hypotension: 10-20 mL 10% calcium gluconate over 10 min, then infusion. Correct Mg first if low. Common in massive transfusion, pancreatitis, rhabdomyolysis, CRRT citrate.

steps.title: Severe (> 14 mg/dL or symptomatic)
steps.detail: 0.9% saline to euvolaemia, then zoledronic acid 4 mg IV (adjust in renal impairment) or calcitonin 4 IU/kg SC for rapid effect; dialysis if renal failure. Look for malignancy, hyperparathyroidism, vitamin D excess.

steps.title: Replace
steps.detail: Mg < 0.7 mmol/L (1.7 mg/dL) or arrhythmia: 2 g MgSO4 IV over 15-60 min; repeat to keep ≥ 0.8-1.0 in cardiac patients.

steps.title: Identify risk
steps.detail: ASPEN: BMI < 16 (severe), weight loss > 7.5% in 3 months or > 10% in 6, negligible intake > 7 days, low baseline K/P/Mg, alcohol use, malignancy, prolonged NPO.

steps.title: Feed carefully
steps.detail: High risk: start 100-150 g dextrose or 10-20 kcal/kg in first 24 h, advance by 33% of goal every 1-2 days. Thiamine 100 mg before feeding and daily for 5-7 days.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.detail: K+, PO4, Mg every 12 h for first 3 days in high-risk patients; if levels fall, replace and do not advance calories.

doseCards.dose: 0.5 mmol/kg over 8-12 h (max ~50 mmol), then recheck
doseCards.verify: Local preparations vary; check mmol/mL and accompanying K+.

tables.title: ASPEN refeeding syndrome severity (fall in P, K or Mg within 5 days of feeding)
columns: Fall in any of P, K, Mg
rows: > 30% and/or organ dysfunction from these deficits or thiamine deficiency
tables.caption: Organ dysfunction includes arrhythmia, respiratory muscle weakness, heart failure, delirium.

redFlags.text: Phosphate < 0.3 mmol/L with weakness, failed weaning or heart failure: replace IV now.

pitfalls.text: Starting full-calorie feeds in a malnourished patient after prolonged starvation.
Using albumin-corrected calcium to decide on calcium therapy in shock or massive transfusion.

pearls.text: Unexplained failure to wean: check phosphate and magnesium.

nodes.text: Thiamine 100 mg; start 10-20 kcal/kg; replace K, P, Mg
P, K or Mg falling (12-hourly × 3 days)?
Advance by 33% of goal every 1-2 days

consultantNotes.evidence: - **ASPEN 2020 consensus:** definitions, risk criteria and a practical feeding protocol.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Malnutrition, alcohol use and prolonged fasting before admission make refeeding risk common in Indian ICUs; tuberculosis patients are a high-risk group.

drugs.name: Balanced crystalloid (Ringer's lactate, Plasma-Lyte)
drugs.indications: Default resuscitation and replacement fluid in most ICU patients.
drugs.adultDose: Resuscitation boluses 250-500 mL over 15-30 min, reassessing after each; replacement matched to measured losses.
drugs.preparationIndia: RL 500 mL bottles/bags (Na 130, K 4, Ca 2.7 mmol/L, lactate 28); Plasma-Lyte A/148 (Na 140, K 5, Mg 1.5, acetate 27, gluconate 23).
drugs.cautions: Mildly hypotonic (RL ~273 mOsm/L): prefer 0.9% saline in raised ICP/severe TBI; volume overload.

drugs.name: 3% sodium chloride
drugs.adultDose: Severe symptoms: 150 mL (or 2 mL/kg) over 20 min, repeat up to 2-3 times checking Na+ between, aiming for +5 mmol/L in the first hours. Limit rise to 10 mmol/L in 24 h (8 if high ODS risk).
drugs.preparationIndia: 3% NaCl (513 mmol/L) bottles available; or locally prepared – confirm recipe and label clearly.
drugs.cautions: Overcorrection and osmotic demyelination; volume overload; peripheral phlebitis with prolonged infusion (short bolus via peripheral line is acceptable).

drugs.name: Calcium gluconate 10%
drugs.indications: Hyperkalaemia with ECG changes; symptomatic hypocalcaemia; calcium channel blocker toxicity; magnesium toxicity.
drugs.adultDose: Hyperkalaemia: 30 mL of 10% IV over 10 min (≈ 6.8 mmol Ca2+), repeat if ECG changes persist. Hypocalcaemia: 10-20 mL over 10 min, then infusion 0.5-1.5 mg/kg/h elemental calcium.
drugs.cautions: Do not mix with bicarbonate (precipitates); caution with digoxin toxicity; extravasation injury.

drugs.name: Insulin + glucose
drugs.adultDose: Soluble insulin 10 units with 25 g glucose IV over 15 min (e.g. 50 mL of 50% dextrose, or 250 mL 10%). If pre-treatment glucose < 7 mmol/L (126 mg/dL), follow with 10% glucose 50 mL/h for 5 h.
drugs.preparationIndia: Regular (soluble) insulin 40 IU/mL vials are common in India; U-100 vials also exist; check the strength.
drugs.cautions: Hypoglycaemia (most common up to 6 h; monitor glucose 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360 min), especially in CKD.

drugs.name: Salbutamol (nebulised)
drugs.adultDose: 10-20 mg nebulised (as additional, not sole therapy).
drugs.cautions: Tachycardia; less effective on β-blockers; caution in ischaemic heart disease.

drugs.name: Potassium chloride
drugs.adultDose: Peripheral: up to 10 mmol/h (40 mmol/L). Central line with cardiac monitoring: up to 20 mmol/h (max 40 mmol/h in life-threatening). Oral 20-40 mmol 2-3 times daily.
drugs.preparationIndia: 15% KCl 10 mL ampoule = 20 mmol. Premixed bags preferred. Never give undiluted or as a bolus.
drugs.cautions: Fatal if pushed; reduce in AKI/oliguria; correct Mg2+.

drugs.name: Magnesium sulphate
drugs.indications: Hypomagnesaemia; refractory hypokalaemia/hypocalcaemia; torsades; eclampsia; severe asthma.
drugs.adultDose: Hypomagnesaemia: 2 g (8 mmol) IV over 15-60 min (over 1-2 min in torsades), then up to 8 g/24 h guided by levels.
drugs.preparationIndia: 50% w/v (2 mmol/mL; 1 g in 2 mL); dilute for infusion.
drugs.cautions: Reduce dose in renal failure; loss of reflexes, respiratory depression if toxic (antidote calcium).

drugs.name: Potassium / sodium phosphate
drugs.adultDose: Moderate (0.3-0.6 mmol/L): 0.3-0.5 mmol/kg IV over 6-12 h; severe (< 0.3): 0.5 mmol/kg (max ~50 mmol) over 8-12 h; recheck.
drugs.preparationIndia: Availability of IV phosphate varies in India; oral phosphate (sodium/potassium phosphate) may be the only option.
drugs.cautions: Hypocalcaemia, metastatic calcification; potassium load; reduce in AKI.
drugs.verify: Check local IV phosphate preparation and its mmol/mL of phosphate and K+/Na+.

verify.reason: Ringer's lactate and 0.9% saline are universal; Plasma-Lyte A/148 and Sterofundin are available in many private hospitals. 3% saline is often prepared locally (e.g. 0.9% saline + 15% or 20% NaCl ampoules); confirm the local recipe.
KCl ampoules in India are commonly 15% w/v (2 mmol/mL, 10 mL = 20 mmol). Never give undiluted; many hospitals use premixed bags.
